articles.title: Ken Atchity, ‘The Meg’ Producer and Literary Agent, Dies at 82
articles.summary: Kenneth Atchity, “The Meg” producer and literary agent, died on Monday. He was 82. Across his career as a literary manager, producer and writer, Atchity produced more than 30 films; wrote over 20 books; negotiated publishing and entertainment deals; and published hundreds of additional titles…
body: Atchity also worked as a communication engineer at AT&T Long Lines, where he designed and implemented the Green Network, which connects NASA’s 26 research centers. He decided to change careers to produce “Shades of Love,” a set of 16 films which were broadcast on HBO and Cinemax and were internationally distributed by Warner Bros..

Born in Eunice, La., in 1944, Atchity was raised in Kansas City, Mo., and attended Georgetown University before entering Yale as a Woodrow Wilson Fellow, where he earned a masters in philosophy and a PhD. While there, his doctoral dissertation won the John Addison Porter prize, the university’s highest academic award, and was published with an introduction by novelist John Gardner.

Atchity is survived by his wife, Kayoko Mitsumatsu; his son, Vincent Atchity; his daughter, Rosemary Atchity; his five grandchildren, Margaret D. McKenna, Edward J. McKenna, Oliver D. Atchity, Eliot J. Atchity and Louis M. Atchity; and his sisters, Mary Calhoun and Laurie Dressman..
Donations may be made to Yoga Gives Back, an organization empowering women and children in India which Atchity served on the board for.

articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen Says Donald Trump Has ‘Elements of Brilliance’ and ‘We Were Too Easy to Dismiss Him as a Nincompoop’
articles.summary: 20 years after retiring Ali G, Sacha Baron Cohen has dusted off his tracksuit collection and reprised the character for “Ali G: Who Iz I?,” now open in theaters before coming to Amazon Prime Oct. 30. The comedian first brought Ali G to audiences at the turn of the century with “Da Ali G Show,”
body: “Later on, I heard that he used to do that with other people,” Baron Cohen said. “It really was a power move.”

Trump appeared taken with Bobin, who Baron Cohen described as a “very handsome, blond, Oxford-educated” Englishman. But when he realized he’d be sitting down with Ali G instead, his demeanor “immediately” changed.

“I actually met a woman who was in the car with him after that interview, and he was apparently furious,” Baron Cohen said. “He actually went out publicly a couple of times to criticize me. And in the end, we used all those clips and used them to advertise another show that I did.”

Baron Cohen’s interview with Trump aired in 2003, back when the future president was best known as a New York real estate mogul, before going on to host NBC’s “The Apprentice.” Looking back at their encounter, Baron Cohen said he could understand how Trump won a second term in the White House, pointing to the president’s “elements of brilliance.”

articles.title: Strictly's new presenters - after frosty reviews have they warmed up?
articles.summary: Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe have split opinion but are getting into the groove, critics say.
body: Strictly Come Dancing's new hosting trio received a very mixed reception when the latest series began a month ago. Ratings have dipped and the jury's still out, but critics say they are slowly getting into the groove.
Changing the hosting team on the BBC's flagship Saturday night entertainment show was never likely to be a waltz in the park.
And going from two presenters to three, and giving them slightly different roles, upset the show's rhythm even more.
Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman were always going to be a hard act to follow.

body: Releasing your first album is a big step for any artist, but for Jazzy it's one that's followed some huge strides.

articles.title: I expect you to cry: what the James Bond actors may face at the final audition
articles.summary: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend. So how can they best prepare? And who is likely to triumph? This weekend, the identity of the next James Bond is finally expected to be known – to the insiders, at least.
body: To say it has been a long time coming is an understatement. It is five years since Daniel Craig was killed in a hail of missiles at the end of No Time to Die, and in that time – even long before it – a swarm of actors have been tipped to replace him, only to age out of the role due to a combination of indecisiveness and cutthroat backstage corporate shenanigans. Whoever is declared to be 007 will be joining the franchise after what is likely to be the longest fallow period in the franchise’s 64-year history.
As such, this is kind of a big weekend. Let’s run through what we know so far.

If three actors are to screen test for Bond this weekend, then they are Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. If there are more – some outlets state that one other actor might be participating, others two – then they won’t include Jack O’Connell or Jacob Elordi, who are both out of the race for one reason or another.

The identity of the other actors are not yet known. Let’s take an uneducated guess and assume that one of them is a Beatle (the best fit is Harris Dickinson) and another one is more famous but less suitable (like Tom Cruise).
points: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend.

articles.title: ‘Fighting an impossible fight is the only way to reclaim dignity’: Lee Chang-dong on class warfare and his searing Oscar contender
articles.summary: The auteur’s new film – a study of labour, capital and the fallout of redundancy – won the grand jury prize at Venice. Telling tales of the disenfranchised is ‘our moral responsibility’, he says. A quintessential 21st-century horror story: a private equity firm has set its sights on your company.
body: In 2009, workers at Ssangyong Motors company protested against plans to lay off between 37 and 43% of the workforce, staging a historic 77-day strike and occupation of the factory that was eventually broken up by riot police. “Until that point in time in Korea, labourers’ rights were widely accepted,” Lee says, speaking through an interpreter in a central London hotel; “however, afterwards, the basic rights of labourers changed; to the public, they couldn’t be seen as more important than market profitability or corporate competitiveness.”

At the time, Lee shelved the project. “The more I examined the pain of these individuals” – after the violent crackdown on the Ssangyong Motors strike, there were several suicides, and reports of long-term mental health issues – “I constantly asked myself: am I worthy of telling this story? And if I am, how do I tell it? Do I stand close to the workers, or keep my distance?” Later he and his co-writer Oh Jung-mi, wrote “many different” scripts, including one with post-apocalyptic elements, before Oh suggested introducing a character who is a documentary film-maker, thereby finding a way to work in Lee’s ambivalence about his intentions.

articles.title: Taika Waititi’s Star Wars film is the latest to hit the buffers. At some point Lucasfilm is going to have to actually make a movie
articles.summary: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet. Movie-making these days is a very expensive endeavour.
body: Perhaps this is one of the reasons why Disney-owned Lucasfilm seems to be so terrified of making new Star Wars movies. Since 2019’s The Rise of Skywalker, only one Star Wars film, the aforementioned Mando and Grogu movie, has actually made it into cinemas. But that has not stopped the studio announcing a small armada of other projects – sometimes via press release, more often at various high-profile celebrations, conferences or other corporate jamborees – that have so far failed to reach multiplexes.

This week, Taika Waititi revealed in an interview with Inverse that his proposed Star Wars film, announced six years ago, has been “put on ice”. No clear explanation was offered, but frankly nobody should be surprised. It now joins mooted projects from Patty Jenkins, Kevin Feige and Game of Thrones creators David Benioff and DB Weiss on the list of Star Wars movies that we were once told we were definitely (probably) getting, but that we never actually did. Some, such as Rian Johnson’s proposed trilogy, have spent years receding into the distance, while others – Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy’s film about Rey’s new Jedi order, anyone? – have never been officially cancelled.
points: Waititi joins a long list of movie-makers who were expected to bring a new direction to the franchise, before the studio appeared to get cold feet.

articles.title: Marvel Reveals New Avengers: Doomsday Footage In Special World Series Commercial
articles.summary: As the hype for Avengers: Doomsday continues to build, Marvel Studios released new footage during Game 1 of the World Series. Check it out here.
body: New footage from "Avengers: Doomsday" has emerged courtesy of the World Series. Marvel Studios unveiled this new glimpse at the upcoming movie during Game 1 of the championship, giving fans a look at previously unseen footage and building yet more hype for one of the most highly-anticipated Marvel releases in years.

Following a series of boring "Doomsday" teaser trailers for which directors the Russo Brothers seemed to have no excuse, Marvel Studios has now managed to build significant hype with some suitably apocalyptic trailers that suggest we'll be in for a grandiose superhero team-up experience. "Doomsday" has already set a major box office record for Marvel months before its December 18, 2026 release, surpassing $50 million in pre-sales 100 days ahead of launch. With the Marvel Cinematic Universe struggling in recent years, this all bodes well for a hugely successful "Doomsday" debut.
